raw_segments.text: Book E, Octavo, Chapter IV, Killer. Of this whale little is precisely known to the Nantucketer
and nothing at all to the professed naturalist. From what I have seen of him at a distance,
I should say that he was about the bigness of a grampus. He is very savage, a sort of
Fiji fish. He sometimes takes the great folio whales by the lip and hangs there like a leech
till the mighty brute is worried to death. The killer is never hunted. I never heard
what sort of oil he has. Exception might be taken to the name bestowed upon this whale,
on the ground of its indistinctness. For we are all killers on land and on sea,
